closed_form_constants_search.caveat_on_K_128_over_105: 128/105 = 2^7/105 is a Wallis-type rational (the family that ordinary beta/Wallis integrals produce). It is NOT a distinguishing fingerprint, and searching for it as prior art is close to meaningless: any hit would almost certainly be a coincidence. For the record, one hit of this shape did occur - arXiv:2208.14711 ('On real roots of polynomials in the context of group theory') contains a Wallis-type sequence beta_n = 2/3, pi/8, 4/15, pi/16, 16/105, 5*pi/128, ... whose fifth term 16/105 is 128/105 divided by 8. NO INFERENCE IS DRAWN FROM THIS. It is the expected behaviour of Wallis rationals, not evidence of prior art.

b_technique_kac_rice_plus_owens_T.verdict: Neither INGREDIENT is novel; the COMBINATION was not found. (1) Non-central Kac-Rice leaving an erf term is Edelman-Kostlan Corollary 5.1 verbatim (see below). (2) Owen's T inside a Rice / level-crossing computation is established (Schwalger 2021; Rawat et al. 2026). (3) No source found uses Owen's T to cancel the erf term and close a Rice-formula computation for a random polynomial, nor to obtain a probability of real-rootedness.

c_edelman_kostlan_1995_reread_MAJOR.what_i_did: Re-downloaded arXiv:math/9501224, ran pdftotext (84 kB), and read Sections 5.2-5.3 in full instead of only grepping for 'probability that all'.
c_edelman_kostlan_1995_reread_MAJOR.corollary_5_1_verbatim_structure: The expected number of real roots of sum a_i f_i(t) = 0 on [a,b] is (1/pi) int_a^b ||gamma'(t)|| e^{-m_0^2(t)/2} [ e^{-m_1^2(t)/2} + sqrt(pi/2) m_1(t) erf(m_1(t)/sqrt2) ] dt, with w = C^{1/2} v, gamma = w/||w||, m_0 = mu/||w||, m_1 = m_0'/||gamma'||.
c_edelman_kostlan_1995_reread_MAJOR.the_key_sentence_verbatim: 'The reader may use this corollary to compute the expected number of roots of a random monic polynomial. In this case m = e_n and C is singular, but this singularity causes no trouble.'
implications: The exact non-central Rice setup for the MONIC ensemble is explicitly flagged in Edelman-Kostlan 1995 as an available application - but is NOT carried out there.
The 'erf/CDF term a naive Rice formula leaves behind' IS literally the erf term of E-K Corollary 5.1. That term is 31 years old and standard.

E-K then isolate exactly two cases where the integral closes: Case I (m_1 == 0: density = constant x mean-zero density) and Case II (m_0 == m_1: closed form (1/4)erf^2(m_0/sqrt2) - (1/(2 sqrt(2 pi))) Gamma[0, m_0^2]). The monic polynomial is in NEITHER case - so E-K closed the easy ones and left the monic one alone.

nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.cite: S. Akiyama, A. Petho, 'On the distribution of polynomials with bounded roots, I. Polynomials with real coefficients', J. Math. Soc. Japan 66(3) (2014); and II (integer coefficients), Unif. Distrib. Theory 9 (2014)
nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.what_they_do: They DO compute exactly, via Selberg-type multiple integrals, the 'probability' that a monic real polynomial is TOTALLY REAL - but in the CONTRACTIVE ensemble (all roots in the unit disc, uniform measure on the coefficient body), with rational answers. Quote from the paper: 'within contractive polynomials, the "probability" of picking a totally real polynomial decreases rapidly when its degree becomes large.'
nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.why_it_is_not_our_result: Different ensemble: bounded-roots/uniform, not iid Gaussian coefficients. Different technique: root-space change of variables + Selberg integrals, not Kac-Rice.
nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.how_found: Cited in the sole answer to MSE 1745310.

nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.cite: Y. Q. Do, N. D. V. Nguyen, S. O'Rourke, 'Real roots of non-centered random polynomials', arXiv:2605.26402 (26 May 2026)
nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.status: closest modern ensemble in spirit (independent coefficients with NON-ZERO means)
nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.what_they_do: Variance asymptotics and CLTs for the number of real roots of non-centered Kac and 'hyperbolic' ensembles; leading variance constant = half the centered one.
nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.checked_how: Downloaded the PDF and grepped: ZERO occurrences of 'monic', ZERO of 'Owen', no all-roots-real probability. Cites Edelman-Kostlan only in the bibliography.
nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.why_it_is_not_our_result: Asymptotic in degree n; no exact low-degree closed form; 'hyperbolic' there means a coefficient ensemble, not real-rootedness.

nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.cite: P. Yatsyna, B. Zmija, 'Counting polynomials with positive roots', arXiv:2509.14501 (2025)
nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.why_not: Monic INTEGER polynomials with all roots real and positive; a counting/asymptotic problem, not a Gaussian probability.

nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.cite: S. A. Sheikh, M. I. Mir, 'Probabilistic Zero Bounds of Certain Random Polynomials', arXiv:2605.25017 (2026)
nearby_ensembles_ruled_out.why_not: Probabilistic Cauchy-type bounds on zero moduli for iid standard-normal coefficients; says nothing about real-rootedness.

stack_exchange_recheck.note: Coefficients uniform on [-N,N], N -> infinity. The single answer sets up the monic cubic x^3+bx^2+cx+d via Vieta and integrates over ROOT space, gets P_3 ~ 0.218 by Monte Carlo, no closed form. Credits the method to Akiyama-Petho.
Uniform [-n,n], n -> infinity; answer gives 41/72 + ln2/12 = 0.6272 (degenerates to the quadratic problem). Not Gaussian.

technique.status: The combination was not found; but BOTH ingredients are prior art and the claim must be scoped accordingly.
not_novel: Non-central Kac-Rice for a Gaussian process with a moving level, leaving an erf term: Edelman-Kostlan 1995, Corollary 5.1 - and they name the monic random polynomial as the intended application.
Closing a non-central Rice integral in closed form: E-K do exactly that for their Case II (erf^2 minus incomplete Gamma).
Owen's T appearing inside Rice / level-crossing computations: Schwalger 2021 (arXiv:2109.07416), Rawat-Morone-Heeger-Martiniani 2026 (arXiv:2605.25278), van Meegen-van Albada 2021.
E[N] = 1 + 2 P(3 real) for a cubic: elementary parity identity, folklore.
not_found_anywhere: Owen's T used as the device that CANCELS the erf/CDF term of the non-central Rice density.
Any Kac-Rice computation of a real-rootedness PROBABILITY (as opposed to an expected count) for a random polynomial.
Any exact evaluation of the monic-Gaussian Kac-Rice integral at any degree.
technique.recommended_phrasing: Claim novelty for the closed form and for the Owen's-T cancellation that produces it. Do NOT claim novelty for 'applying Kac-Rice to the monic Gaussian cubic' - Edelman-Kostlan signposted that in a BAMS survey in 1995 - nor for 'using Owen's T in a Rice-formula context'.

g_verdict_round3.honest_framing: Every statement above is of the form 'I ran query X against corpus Y and it returned nothing'. IA Scholar makes the arXiv/OA negative substantially stronger than in earlier rounds, but it is thin on paywalled mid-20th-century journals and on books, and the one search that would most directly settle the question - literal matching on the integrand - could not be run at all.
